title: UseMutateResult
subtitle: Return type of the useMutate hook
description: Type definition for the object returned by useMutate. Contains the mutation state (isPending, data, error) and functions to trigger the mutation (mutate, mutateAsync) or reset state.

rows.name: isPending
rows.description: True while the mutation is in progress, false otherwise.

rows.name: data
rows.description: The data returned from the last successful mutation. Undefined if no mutation has succeeded yet.

rows.name: error
rows.description: The error from the last failed mutation. Undefined if the last mutation succeeded or no mutation has run.

rows.name: mutate
rows.description: Function to trigger the mutation. Errors are caught internally and stored in the error state.

rows.name: mutateAsync
rows.description: Function to trigger the mutation and return a promise. Throws on error, useful for sequential operations.

rows.name: reset
rows.description: Resets the mutation state to initial values (isPending: false, data: undefined, error: undefined).

examples.description: Accessing mutation state for UI rendering

examples.title: Using mutate vs mutateAsync

behavior.title: mutate vs mutateAsync
behavior.description: mutate catches errors internally, mutateAsync throws them

behavior.title: State Updates
behavior.description: State updates trigger React re-renders automatically

behavior.title: Reset Behavior
behavior.description: reset() clears all state without triggering a new mutation

dos: Use isPending to disable buttons and show loading states
Use mutate() for simple mutations, mutateAsync() when you need the result
Use reset() before showing a form again after success
Check error state to show error messages to users
donts: Don't ignore isPending - always provide loading feedback
Don't use mutateAsync without try/catch if you don't want unhandled rejections
